content:
Rumors suggest Apple's iPhone lineup this fall will revolve around the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra. Below are the three most significant feature differences (excluding price) that may influence your upgrade decision.

Design: Traditional vs. Foldable

This difference is the most obvious, but it's worth highlighting because it's also the most important.

The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max will continue the basic design that has defined the iPhone for years. Reports suggest the screen size and overall design will be identical to the previous generation. If you prefer the feel of a traditional iPhone, the iPhone 18 Pro will be your top choice.

As for the iPhone Ultra, it will be Apple's first foldable model. Its design is entirely different, with an outer display that is shorter and wider than a traditional iPhone, and an inner display similar to the iPad mini.

Camera: Pro Remains the Best in Class

Apple has consistently poured its most cutting-edge and innovative camera technology into the Pro lineup. This year is no exception.

The iPhone Ultra is expected to offer most of the same camera features as the iPhone 18 Pro, but with one major exception: it will not include a telephoto lens.

Sources indicate the iPhone Ultra will feature the same main lens, ultrawide lens, and front-facing camera as the Pro lineup. However, the telephoto lens remains exclusive to the Pro series, and is expected to see further performance improvements this year.

Performance: Both Feature the A20 Pro Chip, but Materials Differ

Both the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra are expected to feature the same A20 Pro chip. However, due to differences in design and materials, performance levels may vary.

The iPhone 18 Pro will retain the same aluminum unibody design as the iPhone 17 Pro, and will also feature a vapor chamber cooling system. These two changes made the iPhone 17 Pro's overall performance significantly better than its predecessor, as the iPhone can maintain lower temperatures under heavy loads.

As for the iPhone Ultra, it will adopt a sleek titanium design similar to the iPhone Air. It may also feature a vapor chamber, but so far only one source has made this claim. However, due to the different materials, even with the same chip as the iPhone 18 Pro, the iPhone Ultra may still deliver slightly lower performance under direct sunlight or when running demanding tasks.
